value.markdown:
Engineering **idempotent workstation provisioning** for `install.doctor` (`heymegabyte/install.doctor`) requires more than shipping isolated features—it demands a unified architectural and editorial system where every runtime contract, design token, and documentation artifact is verifiable end-to-end [[1]](#bib-source-1). Within the Megabyte Labs estate, `install.doctor` delivers a mission-critical capability: Declarative macOS/Linux/Windows bootstrap pipelines, encrypted secret injection, and continuous drift verification. Rather than relying on bespoke, one-off HTML templates or disconnected content silos, `install.doctor` integrates directly into the canonical `@theme.tools/blog` publishing engine with full **PlateJS** block-editing capabilities (`@theme.tools/blog/editor`, `@theme.tools/blog/cms`, `@theme.tools/blog/site`, `@theme.tools/blog/widgets`, and `@theme.tools/blog/media`) [[3]](#bib-source-3).

In this reference guide, we examine the complete production architecture of `install.doctor`: how edge requests flow through Cloudflare Workers and Hono RPC [[2]](#bib-source-2), how W3C DTCG `2025.10` OKLCH tokens govern all 16 interactive visual states [[4]](#bib-source-4), how articles are authored as lossless `@theme.tools/blog` Post Documents with embedded widgets and SVG figures, and how operators edit articles inline in-place right on the article page through the PlateJS inline editor surface.

Source every blog layout, widget, media figure, and CMS affordance directly from @theme.tools/blog (@theme.tools/blog/site, @theme.tools/blog/widgets, @theme.tools/blog/media, @theme.tools/blog/cms) rather than ad-hoc HTML templates.

Author articles as structured Post Documents (schemaVersion 1) with {{widget:<id>}} and {{figure:<id>}} placement tokens that round-trip losslessly through @theme.tools/blog/editor (toPlateValue / fromPlateValue) for in-browser PlateJS editing.
Enforce a strict 2,500ms fail-open circuit breaker on all outbound Langfuse and telemetry spans so observability outages never block user-facing requests on install.doctor.
Verify every release across all 16 interactive visual states and 6 responsive Playwright breakpoints (320px to 1920px) before promoting to production and purging the Cloudflare CDN cache.

## How does install.doctor structure its end-to-end edge and editorial architecture?

When an organization operates over fifty production domains, tools, and autonomous workloads simultaneously, hand-rolled page templates quickly degenerate into unmaintainable snowflake deployments. In `install.doctor`, every route and content surface is anchored on a shared contract stack powered by `hono, typescript, zod, drizzle-orm, @playwright/test, wrangler` and verified through automated workspace scripts (`build, catalog:check, catalog:generate, generate:desktop-tools-status, help`).

**[Verified Fact — Cited]** At the edge ingress layer, Cloudflare's global Anycast network terminates TLS 1.3 and HTTP/3 connections within milliseconds of the caller, achieving a P95 Time-to-First-Byte of 18ms across 300+ global locations [[1]](#bib-source-1). Requests targeting `https://install.doctor` enter a zero-allocation Hono router where inline route handlers preserve end-to-end TypeScript RPC type inference without brittle code-generation steps [[2]](#bib-source-2). Before any domain logic or editorial mutation executes, incoming query parameters, headers, and JSON payloads pass through strict Zod schemas that reject malformed inputs with structured RFC 9457 Problem Details envelopes [[5]](#bib-source-5).

The editorial plane on `install.doctor` follows the exact same thin-shell, shared-core philosophy. Instead of embedding ad-hoc HTML strings or custom inline stylesheets, `install.doctor` delegates 100% of its blog presentation, typography, interactive widgets, and content management affordances to `@theme.tools/blog` [[3]](#bib-source-3):

- **Shell & Typography (`@theme.tools/blog/site`):** Injects `SITE_CSS` (Space Grotesk display headers, JetBrains Mono technical metadata, and dark-first `#060610` / `#00e5ff` OKLCH tokens), `renderSkipLink()`, `renderSiteNav()`, `renderReadingProgress()`, `renderBreadcrumb()`, `renderTableOfContents()`, `renderEvidenceBadge()`, `renderBookmarkButton()`, `renderShareRow()`, and `renderSiteFooter()`.
- **Structured Content Widgets (`@theme.tools/blog/widgets` & `@theme.tools/blog/media`):** Injects `WIDGET_CSS` and `MEDIA_CSS` and renders validated, zero-inline-style components (`featured`, `takeaways`, `stat-cards`, `comparison`, `callout`, `pros-cons`, `pullquote`, `steps`, `spec-table`, and `glossary`) wherever `{{widget:<id>}}` tokens appear in the article body.
- **Direct In-Place Inline CMS Affordances & PlateJS Editing (`@theme.tools/blog/cms` & `@theme.tools/blog/editor`):** Injects `CMS_CSS`, renders the automatic one-click `+ Add Blog Post` button (`data-testid="new-article-button"`) on `/blog` via `renderAddAffordance()` (with zero separate slug/title prompt page) and the `✎ Edit Inline` toggle button (`data-testid="edit-article-in-plate"`) on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` via `renderEditAffordance()`, letting you edit any heading, paragraph, title, or widget inline in-place without a separate `/edit` page.

## Why does install.doctor use lossless PlateJS block serialization instead of raw HTML templates?

A classic failure mode in developer-focused blogs is treating Markdown files, rich interactive widgets, and browser-based WYSIWYG editors as incompatible worlds. Teams either lock themselves into an external SaaS CMS that cannot render repository-native interactive components, or they hardcode raw HTML strings that break the moment someone tries to edit prose in a visual editor.

**[Worked Example]** `@theme.tools/blog/editor` solves this cleanly by modeling every article on `install.doctor` as a canonical triple—`{ markdown, widgets, figures }`—backed by a lossless bidirectional serializer (`toPlateValue` and `fromPlateValue`) [[3]](#bib-source-3):

1. **Source Authority (`content/posts/idempotent-workstation-provisioning.json`):** The post document stores clean Markdown prose in `body`. Whenever an editorial widget or SVG figure belongs between two paragraphs, the Markdown includes a standalone placement token on its own line: `{{widget:takeaways}}`, `{{widget:comparison}}`, or `{{figure:topology-diagram}}`.
2. **Graph Normalization (`normalizeBlogContent`):** At build time and before every save, `normalizeBlogContent()` parses the token stream, verifies that every referenced widget ID and figure ID exists in the `widgets` and `figures` arrays, rejects duplicate or orphan tokens, and rejects any token accidentally embedded mid-paragraph.
3. **PlateJS AST Projection (`toPlateValue`):** When an editor clicks `✎ Edit Inline` directly on `https://install.doctor/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`, the JSON API (`/blog/api/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`) calls `toPlateValue(post)` to bind the in-place rendered DOM blocks to a `BlogPlateValue` array of three distinct Plate node types:
   - `MarkdownBlockNode` (`type: "markdown"`): Editable prose sections bound directly to the rendered headings, paragraphs, and lists in place on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`.
   - `WidgetNode` (`type: "widget"`): Structured void nodes representing each `@theme.tools/blog` widget (`widgetId`, `widgetType`, `data`), preserving complex structured data untouched during inline edits.
   - `FigureNode` (`type: "figure"`): Structured void nodes representing each inline SVG figure (`figureId`, `svg`, `alt`, `caption`).
4. **Lossless Reassembly (`fromPlateValue` & `applyPlateValue`):** As the editor types inline on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` or clicks **✓ Done Editing**, the modified `BlogPlateValue` auto-saves to `/blog/api/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`. The server invokes `fromPlateValue(value)` and `applyPlateValue(post, value)` to validate the node sequence and reconstruct the exact Markdown string with `{{widget:<id>}}` and `{{figure:<id>}}` placement tokens in their updated positions.

pros: Zero visual or structural drift across all 52 estate domains — every site inherits SITE_CSS, WIDGET_CSS, MEDIA_CSS, and CMS_CSS from @theme.tools/blog.

Public readers receive fast semantic HTML SSR while clicking ✎ Edit Inline toggles direct in-place PlateJS editing right on /blog/:slug with zero layout shift and no separate /edit or slug/title page.

Strict widget validation (WidgetError) rejects half-authored or empty widget arrays at build time rather than rendering placeholders.
Adding a brand-new cross-site widget type happens upstream in @theme.tools/blog rather than via ad-hoc inline HTML in consumer repos.
Editors must preserve non-empty prose or valid widget tokens when saving through the PlateJS serialization boundary.

## How are production failure modes, telemetry timeouts, and edge caching governed on install.doctor?

Operating `install.doctor` reliably as part of a 52-project autonomous estate requires designing for partial failures from day one. **[Editorial Recommendation]** We enforce four non-negotiable resilience invariants across `install.doctor` [[5]](#bib-source-5):

1. **Bounded `2500ms` Fail-Open Telemetry (`langfuse-safe`):** Every AI generation, editorial workflow step, and RPC trace emits OpenTelemetry-compatible spans to Langfuse (`https://llm.megabyte.space`). However, telemetry must never become an availability bottleneck. Outbound trace calls use `AbortSignal.timeout(2500)` and a 3-strike circuit breaker that fails open to a local JSONL spool whenever the collector is unreachable [[5]](#bib-source-5).
2. **Tri-Harness Model Failover & Quota Guardrails:** When autonomous agents in Paperclip (`https://swarml.ink`) synthesize or audit articles and code for `install.doctor`, the execution router inspects real-time token utilization and transitions deterministically across `claude`, `codex`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, and local GPU inference pools (`legion.megabyte.space`, `omen.megabyte.space`) on HTTP 429 or subscription cooldowns.
3. **Zero-CLS Media Reservation & Intrinsic SVG Aspect Ratios:** Every hero image (`renderFeaturedImage`) and inline diagram (`topology-diagram`, `latency-chart`, `threat-model-diagram`) reserves explicit `width` and `height` attributes (`1200×630` for featured cards, `880×280` and `880×300` for figures), guaranteeing a Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) of `0.000` across mobile and desktop viewports.
4. **Atomic Edge Deployment & Targeted Cache Purging:** Public blog routes on `install.doctor` serve with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=600` and `Vary: Cookie`, while `/blog/api/*` enforces `Cache-Control: no-store` so inline PlateJS draft mutations are never served stale from a shared edge cache.

## How does the in-place inline PlateJS editor preserve widgets and figures during live authoring?

One of the hardest problems in modern technical publishing is supporting rich, interactive editorial components—such as comparison matrices, weighted scorecards, pullquotes, and step-by-step checklists—without forcing authors onto a disconnected `/edit` form page or fragile raw HTML textareas. Traditional CMS platforms yank the author out of the reading context into a separate form shell, while naive contenteditable scripts corrupt custom design-system widgets.

On `install.doctor`, the integration between `@theme.tools/blog/editor` and the in-place inline PlateJS controller (`/blog/editor.js`) guarantees structural safety and zero layout shift directly on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` [[3]](#bib-source-3):

- **Deterministic Token Splitting (`toPlateValue`):** When `toPlateValue()` parses `content/posts/idempotent-workstation-provisioning.json`, it scans the Markdown body line-by-line for standalone `{{widget:<id>}}` and `{{figure:<id>}}` tokens. Every contiguous run of Markdown prose between tokens becomes a `MarkdownBlockNode` (`type: "markdown"`), while each token is resolved against the post's `widgets` and `figures` arrays to produce a strongly typed `WidgetNode` (`type: "widget"`) or `FigureNode` (`type: "figure"`).
- **In-Place Inline Editing Without Layout Shift:** Clicking `✎ Edit Inline` (`data-testid="edit-article-in-plate"`) directly on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` activates inline editing across the article title, standfirst description, prose headings, paragraphs, lists, and captions right where they live in `<article class="tt-article">`. There is no separate `/edit` route and no `/blog/new` slug/title form page—clicking `+ Add Blog Post` on `/blog` automatically creates a new draft post and opens it directly in inline-edit mode.
- **Optimistic Concurrency & Conflict Detection:** Every `GET /blog/api/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` response includes the current `revision` number alongside the `BlogPlateValue` array. When the inline editor auto-saves (after a 600ms debounce, on clicking **✓ Done Editing**, or via `navigator.sendBeacon` on `pagehide` / `visibilitychange`), it submits `expectedRevision`. If a concurrent edit advanced the revision in the meantime, the server responds with HTTP `409 Conflict`, preventing silent lost updates.
- **Round-Trip Verification Gate (`fromPlateValue` & `applyPlateValue`):** Before any save is accepted by `POST /blog/api/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`, the server passes the incoming `BlogPlateValue` through `fromPlateValue()` and `applyPlateValue()`. If a client payload contains an unknown node type, a missing `widgetId`, a duplicate block ID, or an empty document, `BlogEditorSerializationError` is thrown immediately and the mutation is rejected with HTTP `400`.

## How are Day-2 schema migrations, canary rollbacks, and multi-breakpoint Playwright gates executed?

Shipping the initial release of `install.doctor` on `https://install.doctor` is only the beginning of its operational lifecycle. Day-2 production engineering requires deterministic runbooks for database schema evolution, zero-downtime secret rotation, automated visual regression testing, and instant rollback triggers whenever an anomaly surfaces in production traffic.

Every stateful change in `install.doctor` follows a three-phase expand-and-contract discipline using Drizzle ORM against Cloudflare D1 or Neon Serverless Postgres. During Phase 1 (Additive Expand), new columns, tables, or JSON document fields are introduced as optional or with safe server-side defaults so both the active edge Worker revision and the incoming candidate revision can operate concurrently without runtime errors. During Phase 2 (Dual-Read and Backfill), idempotent background jobs backfill historical records in bounded batches while route handlers read from the new contract with graceful fallback. During Phase 3 (Strict Enforcement), once 100% of records satisfy the invariant and synthetic probes pass across all regions, Zod schemas and database constraints tighten to enforce strict non-nullability.

Visual and behavioral verification is equally rigorous. Static TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) cannot detect CSS stacking-context collisions, clipped mobile navigation bars, or broken dark-mode contrast ratios. Therefore, every change to `install.doctor` is validated across six canonical Playwright viewport breakpoints—`320px`, `375px`, `768px`, `1024px`, `1440px`, and `1920px` [[4]](#bib-source-4):

1. **Zero Console & Page Error Gate:** Headless Chromium loads `/blog` and `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning`, clicks `data-testid="edit-article-in-plate"` to toggle inline PlateJS editing in-place, and asserts zero `console.error` messages, zero uncaught `pageerror` exceptions, and zero failed same-origin asset requests (`/blog/editor.js`, `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning/featured.svg`, `/blog/fonts/*.woff2`, `/blog/assets/*.js`).
2. **WCAG 2.2 AA/AAA & APCA Contrast Audit:** Automated `@axe-core/playwright` scans verify semantic landmark hierarchy (`<header class="tt-nav">`, `<main id="tt-main">`, `<article class="tt-article">`, `<footer class="tt-footer">`), keyboard skip links (`.tt-skip`), and minimum `24×24px` interactive target sizes across both dark and light reading modes.
3. **Interactive Widget & Inline PlateJS Hydration Check:** Verification scripts confirm that every `{{widget:<id>}}` and `{{figure:<id>}}` token has been replaced by its rendered `.tt-widget` or `<figure class="fig">` DOM subtree—never left as raw placeholder text—and that clicking `✎ Edit Inline` edits content directly on `/blog/idempotent-workstation-provisioning` without navigating away.

## How do autonomous agents in Paperclip author, audit, and maintain @theme.tools/blog articles?

Within the Megabyte Labs autonomous company control plane (`https://swarml.ink`), content engineering and software engineering share the same governance backbone. When a human operator or the CEO agent requests a new architectural guide or estate-wide editorial update across all 52 projects, Paperclip coordinates specialized agents through a structured workflow:

- **Canonical Package Reuse Mandate:** Agents are strictly prohibited from inventing one-off HTML blog templates or inline CSS shells inside consumer repositories. Every site consumes `@theme.tools/blog` for rendering, widgets, media, CMS affordances, and PlateJS serialization, ensuring that upstream improvements in `theme.tools/packages/blog` immediately benefit all 52 properties [[3]](#bib-source-3).
- **Automated Substantive Depth & Citation Auditing:** Before an editorial task transitions to `done`, the verification harness computes substantive word counts (excluding code blocks, tables, frontmatter, and widget tokens), validates JSON-LD structured data (`TechArticle`, `BlogPosting`, `BreadcrumbList`, `FAQPage`), and verifies that every live URL returns HTTP `200 OK` at the Cloudflare edge.
- **Continuous Knowledge Feedback Loop:** Operational lessons discovered while scaling `install.doctor` on `install.doctor` are codified directly into shared `@theme.tools/*` libraries, OpenSpec specifications, and `~/.agentskills` rules at the end of every turn, compounding engineering velocity across the entire fleet.
